brief.situation: 10:00 in an outpatient pelvic health clinic. You are the physical therapist. Ms. Chen, 34, is 10 weeks after her second vaginal birth, referred for diastasis recti. She mentions a 'lump at my belly button' that has been sore since yesterday and is not going away.
handover: She has been doing online 'flat belly' curl-ups and lifting her toddler.
Clinic policy: a painful, tender or irreducible abdominal wall bulge goes for same-day surgical assessment; no abdominal exercise until it is cleared.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: What is going on, and what do you do?

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: An inter-rectus distance of 3.5 cm is diastasis recti (over 2 cm is abnormal), but the firm, tender, irreducible, dusky umbilical bulge with nausea and no gas is a possible incarcerated hernia, an emergency.
parts.modelAnswer: She has diastasis recti, 3.5 cm, but that bulge is the urgent thing: firm, tender, won't go back, a bit dusky, and she's nauseated with no gas. That's a possible incarcerated hernia.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: No exercise or forced reduction; emergency department now; tell her obstetric provider; diastasis options (conservative exercise to surgery) after clearance.
parts.modelAnswer: No curl-ups and no pushing on it. Emergency department now, tell her OB provider, and we'll talk diastasis options after.

scoring.modelReasoning: Diastasis recti is an inter-rectus distance over 2 cm at the midline; management ranges from conservative exercise programs to surgery. Before exercise, examine any abdominal wall bulge: a painful hernia that does not get smaller lying down, with nausea, vomiting or a dusky color, may be incarcerated or strangulated and needs urgent surgical care.
